full_judgment: 2. Plaintiffs instituted a suit for permanent injunctions to restrain the defendants from disturbing their possession over the suit land and not to reap away their paddy there from alleging that the suit jote originally belonged to Hosenuddin and it was sold in Certificate Case No. 604/16-17 for arrears of rent and the landlord auction purchased the same and took possession therein and possessed it in khas. The land of the jote thereafter was settled with Safaruddin and Abdul Latif on the basis of a registered kabuliyat dated 16.3.1919. After the settlement Safaruddin and his brother Amjad Ali possessed the lands and after their deaths their heirs had been possessing the lands and paid rents to the landlords. Hosenuddin filed Title Suit No. 242/1919 against the land lord impleading as well Safaruddin and Abdul Latif as defendants for declaration of his raiyati-right in the suit jote and for getting a patta with respect to the suit joie and that suit was dismissed on contest. On appeal as well judgment of the trial Court was affirmed. Thereafter it has been alleged Hosenuddin through his fufatabhai Hasen Ali got instituted the suit for declaration and khas possession on partition being Title Suit No. 88/44 impleading Abdul Latif and Safaruddin, the predecessors of the plaintiffs as defendant nos. 1 and 2 and the landlord as defendant no. 3 and Hosenuddin as pro-defendant no. 4. The learned Munsif dismissed that suit. On appeal, the appellate Court reversed the decree of the learned Munsif and decreed the plaintiffs' suit so far as regards his 8/27th share in the land of schedule 2 except Settlement Plot no. 603. On further appeal to the High Court of Calcutta plaintiffs' right in 8/27th share in plot nos. 417 and 572 was declared and that he would be entitled to recover possession thereof jointly with the defendant. The plaintiffs of the present suit further alleged that heirs of Abdul Latif sold 2.86 acres of land to Noab Ali, son of Hosen Ali and Ansar Ali, son of Aftabuddin. Some of the plaintiffs filed the Misc. Case in Case No. 183/40 for pre-emption of the said kabala up to High Court it was decided in favour of the plaintiffs and the preemptors got pre-emption Dr the kabala land 'width was taken to the High Court in Civil Revision No. 1411/41. The plaintiff alleged that they also purchased some lands of the jote from the heirs of Abdul Latif by kabala dated 29.3.1944. It has been further alleged that subsequent to these kabalas further transactions by way of kabalas took place between the plaintiffs and their heirs. It has been alleged that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land which comprised the bhiti and nal lands and that the defendants have threatened the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit land. The defendant opposite parties 1, 2, 5, 6 and 9 filed written statements and contested the suit. They alleged that the suit land belonged to Hossenuddin and C.S. khatian was correctly recorded in his name and after the death of Hosenuddin his heirs had been possessing the lands. They further denied the certificate sale for arrears of rent of the suit land and delivery of possession in pursuance of the auction sale. They have alleged that the landlords did not lease out the lands to Safaruddin and Abdul Latif and that the kabuliyat was never acted upon if There was no sale of 2.86 acres of land the suit jote out of the jote by Noab Ali, son of Hosenuddin and Ansar All did not purchase 2.86 acres of land out of the suit jote from Abdul Latif Bhuiya and that the alleged pre-emption proceeding at the instance of Anser Ali son of Safaruddin was a collusive one. Defendants have alleged that Hosenuddin possessed the suit jote all through and paid rents to the landlord and after his death his heirs and successors-in-interest have been possessing the same. They have denied the story of auction sale of the jote in certificate sale and taking delivery of possession through Court. The defendants have further alleged that the suit land was unspecified and vague.
